1. General Prover iLock Configuration¶

The configuration of the interlocking application under development, splits into two types:

  1. Generic Application Configuration (GAC)

    This resides below the Prover-iLock-config folder of the top package in the Generic Application (GA),

  2. Specific Application Configuration (SAC)

    This resides below the project folder for each Specific Application (SA).

1.1. Layout Configuration Format¶

The Layout Configuration Format (LCF) is a family of review friendly JSON based configuration file formats, of which 3 are relevant in this context, one generic and two specific ones. These formats normally cover most of the application configuration.

  • The GAC file Types.lcf contains the railyard type system and the list of LCF table headers required in projects using the GA.
  • The SAC file Railyard.lcf contains the railyard layout and all the objects associated to it.
  • The LCF table format is a format for representing SAC data in the form of simple Excel-like tables.

The railyard type system includes all node types in the railyard graph and the user types (and their base types) of all railyard objects.

The set of LCF table headers in the file Types.lcf specify precisely which tables should be present. Each table header specifies a table name identifier, and the names and required types of the columns in the table.

The LCF table format is used to represent the content of the tables declared in Types.lcf.

Each table is either primary or secondary:

  1. Primary tables contain configuration data that is manually reviewed for correctness (even though some consistency checks typically are performed). These are files written and reviewed by the end users when creating the SA. They are given as input to Prover iLock (and Prover Certifier, if used). A typical example of a primary table could be a control table.
  2. Secondary tables contain configuration data that is automatically computed and checked. It consists of information derived from primary tables and the railyard layout. These are internal tables specified and computationally implemented as a part of the GA development. This part of the GA development spans over both Prover iLock and Prover Certifier (if used). Secondary tables are not seen by end users developing the SA; they are internal to the process, both in Prover iLock (and in Prover Certifier). A typical example of a secondary table could be a specification of which track circuits are part of which routes.

2. Package Input¶

2.1. Railyard¶

The package operates on the generic railyard structure defined in Prover-iLock. An instance of this railyard structure is used as input to ILock_Geography. Typically, this instance is either imported from the layout editor in Prover-iLock, or is constructed from external data by some script placed in another package.

A railyard contains minimally the track layout graph, decorated with the objects of the yard. This includes auxiliary data that might not correspond to a physical placement in the yard. The railyard structure also contains two containers, one for paths and one for areas.

Paths can be of arbitrary type and are used to model any sort of path in the track layout that admits continuous train movement: routes, lines, overlaps, etc.

Areas can be of arbitrary type and are used to model any sort of (possibly disconnected) sub-graph of the track layout: interlockings, stations, track circuits, level crossings, etc.

2.2. Primary Tables¶

All the primary LCF tables specified in Types.lcf are required as input.

3. Package Output¶

The main use of the package is to create a PiSPEC instance model of the geography, in Prover-iLock. A PiSPEC instance model consists of

  • named instances of PiSPEC classes,
  • calculated parameters in PiSPEC, and
  • attributes on instances.

One of the main inputs to the process of creating the PiSPEC instance model, is the finalized railyard. It is also an output in its own right, e.g. used with Prover Certifier when performing sign-off verification.

4. Other GA Configuration Files¶

The file graphics.tm that resides in the GDS contains the configuration of the layout editor. It specifies the user types of all objects that are handled in the layout editor. For each user type, it’s graphical type, it’s location in the project, it’s toolbar icon, and it’s vector-graphical presentation in the GUI, is specified.

From the graphical type, the railyard base type of the user type can be inferred. The set of user types and their corresponding base types, is the part from this configuration that has relevance in the context of ILock_Geography.

Note that the user types and base types derived from graphics.tm must be a consistent subset of the user types and base types in Types.lcf.

The file LCF2Inst.lmc describes how to generate PiSPEC instances from the railyard entities.

The file LCF2Par.lmc specifies how to populate the parameters of the generated PiSPEC instances from LCF tables.

The file LCF2Tab.lmc describes how to populate the secondary LCF tables using a set of predefined, Prover Certifier compatible, table methods.

5. Package Content¶

The package provides generic functionality for

  1. searching and calculating in the railyard,
  2. defining and calculating predicates over the railyard (railyard predicates), and
  3. creating a PiSPEC instance model from the railyard.

5.1. Searching and Calculating¶

The package contains a variety of algorithms for searching, in particular for paths and areas. These can be used to specify almost any types of conditions and find all paths or areas satisfying them.

There are also many algorithms for calculating different properties, e.g. overlaps, protection objects, boundaries and intersections of areas.

All of these algorithms are found in geo_algorithms.

One important use of these algorithms is to define and check required railyard properties.

5.2. Defining and Calculating railyard Predicates¶

Railyard predicates are used to describe geographical relationships between instances. They typically appear as parameters of PiSPEC classes.

The package provides a number of Prover Certifier compatible table methods to compute such predicates. The typical way of filling in secondary LCF tables is to specify a table method in a LCF2Tab.lmc file, e.g.:

{
  format: "LCF2Tab-cfg-2.0",
  content: [
    {
      table: "g_normal_in_path",
      method: "SwitchInPathT",
      args: {diverging: false}
    }
  ]
}

The full list of supported table methods is documented in the Table Method Library document.

One could then use the calculated table to fill in PiSPEC instance parameters. How to populate parameters are typically specified in a LCF2Par.lmc file. The example below shows how to populate the require_normal parameter of the PiSPEC class ROUTE_SECTION based on the table g_normal_in_path. Note that both primary and secondary tables may be used to populate parameters.

{
  format: "LCF2Par-cfg-2.0",
  content: [
    {
      dest-param: "ROUTE_SECTION@require_normal",
      lcf-table: "g_normal_in_path"
    }
  ]
}

5.3. Creating PiSPEC Instance Model¶

PiSPEC instances are created from the entities in the railyard. The rules for how to do this are specified in a LCF2Inst.lmc file:

{
  format: "LCF2Inst-cfg-2.0",
  content: [
    {
      user-type: "g_route_section",
      instances: [{dest-type: "ROUTE_SECTION"}]
    }
  ]
}

The example above says that a ROUTE_SECTION instance shall be generated for each railyard entity with user type g_route_section.

6. Package Usage¶

A typical usage process is as follows:

import LCFTableAPI

from iLock_Geography.railyard_import import fromLayoutEditor
import iLock_Geography.lcf.api import LCFWorkflow

railyard fromLayoutEditor(mutable=True).railyard(locked=False)
workflow = LCFWorkflow(railyard, importedLayout=False,
                       useDefaultTypesFile=True)
tables = LCFTableAPI.ParseTables(["/path/to/tables.lcf"])[0].Tables
for table in tables:
  workflow.addPrimaryTable(table)
workflow.modifyRailyard(callback_that_adds_objects)
workflow.addLCF2Inst("/path/to/LCF2Inst.lmc")
workflow.addLCF2Par("/path/to/LCF2Par.lmc")
workflow.addLCF2Tab("/path/to/LCF2Tab.lmc")
workflow.run()

  1. Creation of initial railyard

    Create the initial railyard graph by importing it from file or, more typically, by retrieving it from the layout editor using a call to the iLock_Geography API (railyard_import.fromLayoutEditor).

  2. Create a LCFWorkflow object

    This object manages the creation of PiSPEC instances in accordance to the provided configuration files.

  3. Load primary LCF tables

    Import all the primary LCF tables to be used for extending the railyard or calculating parameters.

  4. Creation of finalized railyard

    Finalize the railyard structure by optionally using algorithms in the package (located in geo_algorithms) and/or data from the primary LCF tables for finding more paths and/or finding more areas.

    Check that the railyard satisfies required properties, using algorithms in the package.

  5. Add configuration files for generating PiSPEC

    This includes adding any LCF2Inst.lmc, LCF2Par.lmc and LCF2Tab.lmc files.

  6. Call LCFWorkflow.run to generate the PiSPEC instances
